title: AlignedNorm: Prompting Vision–Language Models via Coupled Prompt Field
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: Optimizing tasks in isolation leaves their targets misaligned; coupling them in one shared field pulls both toward a common optimum.
layout: 2 stacked panels, top-to-bottom, dashed divider, vector-field streamlines with legend
description: Two vertically stacked toy 2-D vector-field sketches separated by a bold dashed horizontal line. Top panel, labeled 'Isolated Optimization', shows orange circles (Base) on the left with streamlines flowing right toward a hollow triangle (Target). Red squares (New) on the right flow along a curved path to a different point, away from the triangle. A red dashed line and a curved black arrow are labeled 'Misaligned'. Bottom panel, labeled 'Coupled Prompt Field', shows the same orange circles and red squares moving along straight, opposing arrows toward the central triangle. A curved double-headed arrow labeled 'Coupled' links the two groups. A legend at the right gives Base, New and Target. Faint dashed gray streamlines fill the background, and the contrast between scattered and converging points draws the eye first.
caption: Our coupled prompt field. We couple Base and New
abstract: Prompt learning for vision-language models (VLMs) primarily follows end-to-end or decoupled routes to balance base and new task performance, but suffers a fundamental bottleneck: sample-wise optimization within task-specific feature spaces traps models in local optima, hindering global optimality. To address this, we identify a key insight that VLMs can be prompted within a Coupled Prompt Field-a shared space where base and new tasks are mutually constrained-and present AlignedNorm, which enforces the field coupling. By dynamically aligning the norms of prompts to VLMs' native scale, our method enables joint optimization of both tasks. Without complex designs, our method matches leading decoupled approaches on 15 datasets across 4 experimental settings, offering both a new perspective and a practical solution to the local-optima dilemma in prompt learning.
